  deploy-vps:
    name: Deploy to Staging VPS
    needs: [build-api, build-tee, build-web]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - name: Download web dist artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: web-dist
          path: web-dist/

      - name: Generate .env.staging
        run: |
          cat > .env.staging << 'ENVEOF'
          NODE_ENV=staging
          CIPHERBOX_ENVIRONMENT=staging
          TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=${{ secrets.STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET }}
          PORT=3000
          DB_HOST=postgres
          DB_PORT=5432
          DB_USERNAME=${{ vars.STAGING_DB_USERNAME }}
          DB_PASSWORD=${{ secrets.STAGING_DB_PASSWORD }}
          DB_DATABASE=cipherbox_staging
          JWT_SECRET=${{ secrets.STAGING_JWT_SECRET }}
          CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=${{ vars.CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS }}
          IPFS_PROVIDER=local
          IPFS_LOCAL_API_URL=http://ipfs:5001
          IPFS_LOCAL_GATEWAY_URL=http://ipfs:8080
          DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=https://delegated-ipfs.dev
          REDIS_HOST=redis
          REDIS_PORT=6379
          TEE_WORKER_URL=http://tee-worker:3001
          TEE_WORKER_SECRET=${{ secrets.STAGING_TEE_WORKER_SECRET }}
          REDIS_PASSWORD=${{ secrets.STAGING_REDIS_PASSWORD }}
          GRAFANA_LOKI_URL=${{ vars.GRAFANA_LOKI_URL }}
          GRAFANA_LOKI_USERNAME=${{ vars.GRAFANA_LOKI_USERNAME }}
          GRAFANA_LOKI_API_KEY=${{ secrets.GRAFANA_LOKI_API_KEY }}
          GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_URL=${{ vars.GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_URL }}
          GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_USERNAME=${{ vars.GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_USERNAME }}
          GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_API_KEY=${{ secrets.GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_API_KEY }}
          SENDGRID_API_KEY=${{ secrets.SENDGRID_API_KEY }}
          SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL=${{ vars.SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL }}
          GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=${{ vars.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }}
          IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY=${{ secrets.IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          ENVEOF
          # Append image tag and lowercase owner (can't use shell vars in quoted heredoc)
          OWNER="${{ github.repository_owner }}"
          echo "GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER=${OWNER,,}" >> .env.staging
          echo "TAG=${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}" >> .env.staging

      - name: Copy files to VPS
        uses: appleboy/scp-action@v0.1.7
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.STAGING_HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.STAGING_USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.STAGING_SSH_KEY }}
          source: '.env.staging,docker/docker-compose.staging.yml,docker/Caddyfile,docker/alloy-config.river'
          target: /opt/cipherbox
          strip_components: 0

      - name: Arrange files on VPS
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1.2.0
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.STAGING_HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.STAGING_USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.STAGING_SSH_KEY }}
          script: |
            # Move files to correct locations
            mv /opt/cipherbox/.env.staging /opt/cipherbox/docker/.env.staging 2>/dev/null || true
            cd /opt/cipherbox/docker

            # Docker Compose reads .env automatically for variable substitution
            cp .env.staging .env

            # Restrict env file permissions (contains secrets)
            chmod 600 .env .env.staging

            # Ensure certs symlink exists for Caddy
            rm -rf /opt/cipherbox/docker/certs
            ln -sf /opt/cipherbox/certs /opt/cipherbox/docker/certs

      - name: Deploy web app files to VPS
        uses: appleboy/scp-action@v0.1.7
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.STAGING_HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.STAGING_USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.STAGING_SSH_KEY }}
          source: 'web-dist/*'
          target: /opt/cipherbox/web
          strip_components: 1
          rm: true

      - name: Deploy services
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1.2.0
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.STAGING_HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.STAGING_USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.STAGING_SSH_KEY }}
          script: |
            set -euo pipefail
            cd /opt/cipherbox/docker

            # Login to GHCR
            echo "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" | docker login ghcr.io -u ${{ github.actor }} --password-stdin

            # Set image tag from git tag (GHCR requires lowercase owner)
            export TAG="${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}"
            OWNER="${{ github.repository_owner }}"
            export GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER="${OWNER,,}"

            # Pull new images
            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml pull

            # Run database migrations before starting services
            # (api service inherits env vars from env_file in compose)
            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml run --rm \
              api node dist/run-migrations.js

            # Start/restart services
            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml up -d

            # Restart Caddy to pick up refreshed web files bind mount
            # (scp rm:true recreates the host dir, breaking the old mount inode)
            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml restart caddy

            # Cleanup old images
            docker image prune -f

  provision-dashboard:
    name: Provision Grafana Dashboard
    needs: [deploy-vps]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - name: Push dashboard to Grafana Cloud
        env:
          GRAFANA_URL: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_URL }}
          GRAFANA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GRAFANA_API_KEY }}
          DS_METRICS_UID: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_DS_METRICS_UID }}
          DS_LOGS_UID: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_DS_LOGS_UID }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          : "${GRAFANA_URL:?GRAFANA_URL is required}"
          : "${GRAFANA_API_KEY:?GRAFANA_API_KEY is required}"
          : "${DS_METRICS_UID:?GRAFANA_DS_METRICS_UID is required}"
          : "${DS_LOGS_UID:?GRAFANA_DS_LOGS_UID is required}"

          # The dashboard JSON uses __inputs for datasource templating.
          # Replace variable references with actual datasource UIDs.
          DASHBOARD=$(cat docker/grafana/dashboards/cipherbox-staging.json \
            | jq --arg metrics "$DS_METRICS_UID" --arg logs "$DS_LOGS_UID" \
                 'del(.__inputs)
                  | .id = null
                  | walk(if type == "object" and .uid? and (.uid | test("\\$\\{DS_")) then
                      .uid = (if .uid == "${DS_GRAFANA_CLOUD_METRICS}" then $metrics
                              elif .uid == "${DS_GRAFANA_CLOUD_LOGS}" then $logs
                              else .uid end)
                    else . end)')

          # Fail if any datasource placeholder survived the rewrite
          if jq -e '.. | objects | .uid? | select(type == "string" and test("^\\$\\{DS_"))' \
            >/dev/null <<<"$DASHBOARD"; then
            echo "::error::Unresolved datasource placeholder(s) remain in dashboard JSON"
            exit 1
          fi

          # Wrap in import payload
          PAYLOAD=$(jq -n --argjson dashboard "$DASHBOARD" '{
            dashboard: $dashboard,
            overwrite: true,
            message: "Provisioned by deploy-staging workflow"
          }')

          # Push to Grafana API
          HTTP_CODE=$(curl -sS --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 60 \
            -o /tmp/grafana-response.json -w "%{http_code}" \
            -X POST "${GRAFANA_URL}/api/dashboards/db" \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${GRAFANA_API_KEY}" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d "$PAYLOAD")

          if [[ ! "$HTTP_CODE" =~ ^2[0-9][0-9]$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::Grafana API returned HTTP $HTTP_CODE"
            cat /tmp/grafana-response.json
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "Dashboard provisioned successfully (HTTP $HTTP_CODE)"
          jq -r '.url // "unknown"' /tmp/grafana-response.json

lines: # The dashboard JSON uses __inputs for datasource templating.
# Replace variable references with actual datasource UIDs.

input.command:
git add .github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix: strip trailing slash from GRAFANA_URL to prevent 301 redirect

Grafana Cloud returns HTTP 301 when the URL has a double slash
(e.g. https://host//api/...). Strip trailing slash defensively.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git push -u origin fix/grafana-trailing-slash
input.description: Commit, push, and set upstream for new branch

content.text:
**Root cause:** `GRAFANA_URL` was set to `https://cipherbox.grafana.net/` (trailing slash), so the curl request hit `https://cipherbox.grafana.net//api/dashboards/db` — Grafana returned a **301 redirect** to the canonical single-slash path, and `curl` doesn't follow redirects by default.

**Fix (two-pronged):**
1. Updated the `GRAFANA_URL` GitHub variable to remove the trailing slash
2. Added `GRAFANA_URL="${GRAFANA_URL%/}"` in the script as a defensive strip

content.text:
The URL is now correct (no double slash), but the response body is just `{}` with a 403. A few things to check beyond the API key itself:

1. **API key type** — Grafana Cloud uses **Service Account tokens**, not the legacy API keys. In Grafana Cloud:
   - Go to **Administration > Service Accounts** (not the old "API Keys" page)
   - Create a service account with **Editor** role (or Admin)
   - Generate a token for that service account
   - The token should start with `glsa_` (Grafana Cloud service account) — if yours starts with `eyJ` or something else, it's the wrong type

2. **Permissions** — The token needs **Editor** or **Admin** role. A Viewer token would return 403 on dashboard writes.

3. **Authorization header format** — The script uses `Bearer ${GRAFANA_API_KEY}`. Grafana Cloud service account tokens use `Bearer glsa_...` which is correct. But if you're using basic auth credentials (username:password from the Grafana Cloud portal), those need `Basic` auth instead, not `Bearer`.

4. **URL target** — Make sure `https://cipherbox.grafana.net` is the Grafana instance URL, not the Prometheus/Loki push endpoint. You can verify by opening `https://cipherbox.grafana.net/api/dashboards/home` in a browser.

**Most likely culprit**: The secret stored in `GRAFANA_API_KEY` is either the basic auth password from the Grafana Cloud data source config (not a service account token) or a Viewer-level token. You need a **service account token with Editor role** from Grafana Cloud > Administration > Service Accounts.
I will rotate the api key, but want to make sure the service account configs are right first

The service account config looks correct:

- **Role:** Editor — sufficient for `POST /api/dashboards/db`
- **Token:** "github actions token" — never expires, and "Last used at" shows it was actually used during the failed run, so the token is reaching Grafana

Since the token was used (last used matches the run time) but returned 403, the issue is likely that the **token value stored in the GitHub secret doesn't match the current token**. Maybe it was copy-pasted with extra whitespace, or an older token was stored before this service account was configured correctly.

Go ahead and rotate — delete the existing token, create a new one, and update the `GRAFANA_API_KEY` secret in GitHub. Make sure the value starts with `glsa_` and has no leading/trailing whitespace.

The key thing: this is **Grafana Cloud**, not self-hosted. Grafana Cloud has an additional access control layer. A few things to check:

1. **Use the Grafana Cloud Stack API URL, not the instance URL.** In Grafana Cloud, the API endpoint might need to be `https://cipherbox.grafana.net` (which you have), but some orgs require going through `https://grafana.com/api/...` instead.

2. **Try upgrading the service account role to Admin** — Editor _should_ work for `/api/dashboards/db`, but on Grafana Cloud the RBAC may differ. You can test this quickly.

3. **Check if there's an org-level API access restriction.** In Grafana Cloud: go to **Administration > General > API access** — some orgs have API access disabled or restricted to specific IPs.

4. **Quick local test** — you can verify the token works from your machine:

```bash
curl -sS -w "\n%{http_code}" \
  -X GET "https://cipherbox.grafana.net/api/org" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"
```

If that also returns 403, the issue is at the Grafana Cloud level, not the workflow. If it returns 200, we know the token works and there may be an IP/network restriction on the Cloud side.

input.content:
# Grafana Cloud Dashboard Provisioning via API

**Date:** 2026-03-07

## Original Prompt

> Set up auto-provisioning of Grafana dashboards on staging deploys so dashboard changes in the repo automatically push to Grafana Cloud.

## What I Learned

- **Grafana Cloud requires Admin role for dashboard API writes.** The service account Editor role returns 403 on `POST /api/dashboards/db`, even though Grafana OSS docs say Editor is sufficient. This is a Grafana Cloud RBAC quirk.
- **Trailing slashes in the Grafana URL cause 301 redirects.** `curl` does not follow redirects by default, so `https://host//api/...` (double slash from trailing slash + path) silently fails with HTTP 301. Always strip trailing slashes defensively: `GRAFANA_URL="${GRAFANA_URL%/}"`.
- **The 403 response body is just `{}`** — no error message, no hint about permissions. The only way to diagnose is to check the service account role and test with a local curl.
- **Dashboard JSON `__inputs` need runtime substitution.** Grafana export includes `__inputs` for datasource templating with `${DS_*}` placeholder UIDs. These must be replaced with actual datasource UIDs at import time using `jq walk()`.
- **`environment: staging` is required on GitHub Actions jobs** that reference env-scoped vars/secrets. Without it, `vars.*` and `secrets.*` resolve to empty strings silently.

## What Would Have Helped

- Knowing upfront that Grafana Cloud RBAC differs from self-hosted Grafana for API access
- A quick local `curl` test of the token before wiring it into CI would have caught the 403 immediately
- Checking the Grafana URL for trailing slash before the first deploy

## Key Files

- `.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml` — `provision-dashboard` job
- `docker/grafana/dashboards/cipherbox-staging.json` — dashboard source of truth

# Performance Baselines - Phase 18

## Capture Information

| Field            | Value                                                    |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Capture Date** | TBD -- run baseline-benchmark.sh on staging after deploy |
| **Environment**  | Staging (api-staging.cipherbox.cc)                       |
| **Kubo Version** | v0.34.0                                                  |
| **API Image**    | TBD (tag from deploy)                                    |
| **VPS**          | Hostinger 76.13.151.200, 4 vCPU, 8GB RAM                 |
| **Script**       | `scripts/baseline-benchmark.sh`                          |
| **Iterations**   | 20 measured + 3 warmup per operation                     |
| **File Size**    | 10KB random data (upload/download)                       |

## Methodology

Baselines are captured using `scripts/baseline-benchmark.sh` which:

1. Discovers the user's root IPNS name via `GET /vault`
2. Runs 3 warmup iterations (discarded) followed by 20 measured iterations
3. Measures client-side round-trip time via `curl -w "%{time_total}"`
4. Computes p50/p95/p99 from sorted timing values
5. IPNS Publish is excluded (requires signed record) -- captured from Prometheus

Server-side histograms (`cipherbox_ipfs_ipns_duration_seconds`) provide internal timing without network overhead. Client-side timings from this script include network latency and are useful for end-to-end comparison.

## Client-Side Timings (curl round-trip)

| Operation           | p50 | p95 | p99 | Notes                                   |
| ------------------- | --- | --- | --- | --------------------------------------- |
| IPNS Resolve        | TBD | TBD | TBD | `GET /ipns/resolve?ipnsName=<name>`     |
| IPNS Publish        | --  | --  | --  | See Prometheus (requires signed record) |
| IPFS Pin (upload)   | TBD | TBD | TBD | `POST /ipfs/upload` with 10KB file      |
| IPFS Cat (download) | TBD | TBD | TBD | `GET /ipfs/<cid>` for 10KB file         |

## Server-Side Histograms (Prometheus)

Captured from Grafana Cloud after sufficient organic staging usage.

| Metric                                       | Operation  | p50 | p95 | p99 | Notes                 |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------- | --- | --- | --- | --------------------- |
| `cipherbox_ipfs_ipns_duration_seconds`       | resolve    | TBD | TBD | TBD | Source: db vs network |
| `cipherbox_ipfs_ipns_duration_seconds`       | publish    | TBD | TBD | TBD |                       |
| `cipherbox_ipfs_ipns_duration_seconds`       | pin        | TBD | TBD | TBD |                       |
| `cipherbox_ipfs_ipns_duration_seconds`       | cat        | TBD | TBD | TBD |                       |
| `cipherbox_republish_batch_duration_seconds` | batch      | TBD | TBD | TBD | TEE provider: mock    |
| `cipherbox_http_request_duration_seconds`    | all routes | TBD | TBD | TBD | Existing dashboard    |

## HTTP API Performance (from existing dashboard)

| Route                | p50 | p95 | p99 | Notes               |
| -------------------- | --- | --- | --- | ------------------- |
| `POST /ipfs/upload`  | TBD | TBD | TBD |                     |
| `GET /ipfs/:cid`     | TBD | TBD | TBD |                     |
| `GET /ipns/resolve`  | TBD | TBD | TBD |                     |
| `POST /ipns/publish` | TBD | TBD | TBD |                     |
| Overall              | TBD | TBD | TBD | All routes combined |

## Kubo Health Observations

| Metric             | Value | Notes                                                                                        |
| ------------------ | ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Peer Connections   | TBD   | `libp2p_swarm_connections_opened_total - closed_total` or manual `ipfs swarm peers \| wc -l` |
| Inbound Bandwidth  | TBD   | `rate(libp2p_network_in_bytes_total)` -- may need manual check if metric unavailable         |
| Outbound Bandwidth | TBD   | `rate(libp2p_network_out_bytes_total)`                                                       |
| Memory Usage       | TBD   | `go_memstats_alloc_bytes`                                                                    |
| Goroutines         | TBD   | `go_goroutines`                                                                              |
| Datastore Size     | TBD   | Check via `ipfs repo stat` if no Prometheus metric available                                 |

## Notes

- All TBD values will be filled after Phase 18 code is deployed to staging
- IPNS Publish baseline requires organic usage or E2E test runs to populate histogram buckets
- Kubo v0.34.0 may not expose all libp2p metrics -- fallback metrics noted in Kubo Health section
- These baselines will be compared against Phase 22 (post-architectural-change) measurements
- The benchmark script is deterministic: same iterations, same file size, same warmup count

## Comparison Target

Phase 22 (after IPFS infrastructure changes) will re-run this benchmark and document:

- Performance regression threshold: >20% p95 increase requires investigation
- Performance improvement targets vary by operation (see Phase 22 plan)

Looking at the dashboard, I can see:

1. **IPFS Pin/Cat Duration** - Has some data (the chart shows lines) but the IPNS panels show "No data" for publishes and resolve/publish duration
2. **IPNS Publishes Over Time** - "No data"
3. **IPNS Resolve/Publish Duration** - "No data"

5. **Kubo Health** - All "No data"

The benchmark script only exercised resolve, upload, and download - but the Prometheus histograms for these operations apparently aren't showing data either. This is odd - the IPFS Pin/Cat Duration chart does show some lines though.


The real issue is that IPNS publishes aren't being triggered by the benchmark, and the server-side instrumentation might not be recording properly. I should run the E2E tests against staging to generate actual usage patterns, since those would exercise the full upload and folder creation flows that trigger IPNS publishes.

The E2E tests are hardcoded to `localhost:5173` and start local servers. Running them against staging would need overriding `baseURL` and skipping the `webServer` setup. We can do that with env vars:

```bash
cd tests/e2e && BASE_URL=https://app-staging.cipherbox.cc \
  pnpm exec playwright test --config=- <<< "..." 
```

Actually, simpler approach — let me just run the benchmark script a few more times plus use Playwright MCP to do some real file operations on staging to trigger IPNS publishes. The benchmark alone won't trigger publishes since that requires uploading files through the full web app flow (which updates the IPNS record).

Let me run the benchmark 3 more times in the background to generate more histogram data for resolve/pin/cat, and simultaneously use Playwright to do file operations that trigger IPNS publishes.

content.text:
The JWT token alone isn't enough — the app also needs Web3Auth session state for the crypto key derivation. Injecting a token into localStorage won't work without the full Web3Auth session.

This approach won't work via Playwright against staging since the OTP flow fails (test account OTP likely only works against the local dev Web3Auth configuration). 

Let me try a different approach — use the API directly to simulate file operations that trigger IPNS publishes. The publish happens server-side when the client calls `POST /ipns/publish` after uploading.

content.text:
The publish endpoint requires a signed IPNS record from the client — which needs the IPNS private key that's encrypted and only available client-side after Web3Auth key derivation. We can't forge that from the API alone.

The realistic options are:

1. **Wait for organic usage** — the republish cron runs every 3 hours, so it will eventually generate publish data
2. **Trigger the republish job manually** — if there's a way to trigger the BullMQ job
3. **You log into staging manually** and do a few file uploads — that triggers the publish flow

Let me check if there's a way to trigger the republish cron.

content.text:
The snapshot doesn't embed query results in the new dashboard format — the data is loaded live from Prometheus (which fails with 401 for anonymous users, explaining the error logs). The table panels seem to work because they're simpler.

The best data I have is from the **Response Time by Route (p95)** table which gives us actual server-side HTTP response times. This is solid enough — it's from the `cipherbox_http_request_duration_seconds` histogram.

Here's what we pulled from the Grafana dashboard:

## Server-Side Performance Data (from Grafana)

**HTTP Response Time by Route (p95) — Mean / Max over 6h window:**

| Route | p95 Mean | p95 Max |
|-------|----------|---------|
| `POST /ipfs/upload` | 328 ms | 1.67 s |
| `GET /ipfs/:cid` | 9.50 ms | 9.50 ms |
| `GET /ipns/resolve` | 286 ms | 887 ms |
| `POST /ipns/publish` | **860 ms** | **919 ms** |
| `POST /ipns/publish-batch` | 813 ms | 950 ms |
| `GET /vault` | 9.50 ms | 9.50 ms |
| `GET /vault/quota` | 9.50 ms | 9.50 ms |

**Key findings:**
- **IPNS Publish is the slowest operation** at ~860ms p95 — this is the data we were missing
- IPNS Resolve at 286ms p95 server-side vs 224ms client-side (benchmark) — reasonable 
- IPFS cat is extremely fast server-side (9.5ms) — the ~133ms client-side timing is mostly network latency
- IPFS upload p95 at 328ms mean, spiking to 1.67s for larger files

The TEE Republish Batch Duration panel shows "No data" — the mock TEE provider likely doesn't report real durations. Kubo Health panels also show "No data" (Kubo doesn't expose those libp2p metrics as noted in the baselines doc).

Want me to update the baselines document with these server-side values?

| **File Size**    | 10KB random data (upload/download)       |

## Methodology

Baselines are captured using `scripts/baseline-benchmark.sh` which:

1. Discovers the user's root IPNS name via `GET /vault`
2. Runs 3 warmup iterations (discarded) followed by 20 measured iterations
3. Measures client-side round-trip time via `curl -w "%{time_total}"`
4. Computes p50/p95/p99 from sorted timing values
5. IPNS Publish is excluded (requires signed record) -- captured from Prometheus

Server-side histograms (`cipherbox_ipfs_ipns_duration_seconds`) provide internal timing without network overhead. Client-side timings from this script include network latency and are useful for end-to-end comparison.

## Client-Side Timings (curl round-trip)

| `cipherbox_http_request_duration_seconds`    | all routes | TBD | TBD | TBD | Existing dashboard    |

## HTTP API Performance (from existing dashboard)

| **Iterations**   | 20 measured + 3 warmup per operation     |
| **File Size**    | 10KB random data (upload/download)       |

## Methodology

Baselines are captured using `scripts/baseline-benchmark.sh` which:

1. Discovers the user's root IPNS name via `GET /vault`
2. Runs 3 warmup iterations (discarded) followed by 20 measured iterations
3. Measures client-side round-trip time via `curl -w "%{time_total}"`
4. Computes p50/p95/p99 from sorted timing values
5. IPNS Publish is excluded (requires signed record) -- captured from Prometheus

Server-side histograms (`cipherbox_ipfs_ipns_duration_seconds`) provide internal timing without network overhead. Client-side timings from this script include network latency and are useful for end-to-end comparison.

## Client-Side Timings (curl round-trip)

| ------------------- | ------ | ------ | ------ | --------------------------------------- |

| IPFS Pin (upload)   | 0.138s | 0.218s | 0.227s | `POST /ipfs/upload` with 10KB file      |
| IPFS Cat (download) | 0.133s | 0.215s | 0.219s | `GET /ipfs/<cid>` for 10KB file         |

| `cipherbox_ipfs_ipns_duration_seconds`       | pin        | --  | --   | --   | See HTTP table below (internal metric TBD)     |
| `cipherbox_ipfs_ipns_duration_seconds`       | cat        | --  | --   | --   | See HTTP table below (internal metric TBD)     |
| `cipherbox_republish_batch_duration_seconds` | batch      | --  | --   | --   | No data (mock TEE provider doesn't report)     |
| `cipherbox_http_request_duration_seconds`    | all routes | --  | see below | -- | Per-route breakdown in HTTP table         |

Note: The internal `cipherbox_ipfs_ipns_duration_seconds` histogram values could not be extracted from the Grafana snapshot (new dashboard format does not embed query results for anonymous viewers). The per-route HTTP duration histogram below provides equivalent server-side timing data.

## HTTP API Performance (from Grafana dashboard)

Response Time by Route (p95) — mean and max over 6h window (12:30–18:30 UTC):

| Route                     | p95 Mean | p95 Max | Notes                                   |
| ------------------------- | -------- | ------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `POST /ipfs/upload`       | 328 ms   | 1.67 s  | Includes 1MB/5MB/10MB uploads           |

| `POST /auth/test-login`   | 177 ms   | 243 ms  |                                         |

- p50: ~10 ms (most routes are fast DB lookups)
- p95: ~300 ms (dominated by IPNS resolve)
- p99: ~900 ms (dominated by IPNS publish, spikes to ~3s under load)

# Performance Baselines - Phase 18

## Capture Information

| Field            | Value                                    |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| **Capture Date** | 2026-03-07T16:55:31Z (updated 2026-03-07T17:30Z) |
| **Environment**  | Staging (api-staging.cipherbox.cc)       |
| **Kubo Version** | v0.34.0                                  |
| **API Image**    | v0.24.2-staging-rc-1                     |
| **VPS**          | Hostinger 76.13.151.200, 4 vCPU, 8GB RAM |
| **Script**       | `scripts/baseline-benchmark.sh`          |
| **Iterations**   | 20 measured + 3 warmup per operation     |
| **File Size**    | 10KB random data (upload/download)       |

## Methodology

Baselines are captured using `scripts/baseline-benchmark.sh` which:

1. Discovers the user's root IPNS name via `GET /vault`
2. Runs 3 warmup iterations (discarded) followed by 20 measured iterations
3. Measures client-side round-trip time via `curl -w "%{time_total}"`
4. Computes p50/p95/p99 from sorted timing values
5. IPNS Publish is excluded (requires signed record) -- captured from Prometheus

Server-side histograms (`cipherbox_ipfs_ipns_duration_seconds`) provide internal timing without network overhead. Client-side timings from this script include network latency and are useful for end-to-end comparison.

## Client-Side Timings (curl round-trip)

| Operation           | p50    | p95    | p99    | Notes                                   |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------ | ------ | --------------------------------------- |
| IPNS Resolve        | 0.147s | 0.224s | 0.278s | `GET /ipns/resolve?ipnsName=<name>`     |
| IPNS Publish        | --     | --     | --     | See Prometheus (requires signed record) |
| IPFS Pin (upload)   | 0.138s | 0.218s | 0.227s | `POST /ipfs/upload` with 10KB file      |
| IPFS Cat (download) | 0.133s | 0.215s | 0.219s | `GET /ipfs/<cid>` for 10KB file         |

## Server-Side Histograms (Prometheus)

Captured from Grafana Cloud dashboard snapshot after stress test (~43 UI operations + 60 benchmark iterations).
Snapshot: `CipherBox Staging - 2026-03-07 18:30`

| Metric                                       | Operation  | p50 | p95  | p99  | Notes                                          |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------- | --- | ---- | ---- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `cipherbox_ipfs_ipns_duration_seconds`       | resolve    | --  | --   | --   | See HTTP table below (internal metric TBD)     |
| `cipherbox_ipfs_ipns_duration_seconds`       | publish    | --  | --   | --   | See HTTP table below (internal metric TBD)     |
| `cipherbox_ipfs_ipns_duration_seconds`       | pin        | --  | --   | --   | See HTTP table below (internal metric TBD)     |
| `cipherbox_ipfs_ipns_duration_seconds`       | cat        | --  | --   | --   | See HTTP table below (internal metric TBD)     |
| `cipherbox_republish_batch_duration_seconds` | batch      | --  | --   | --   | No data (mock TEE provider doesn't report)     |
| `cipherbox_http_request_duration_seconds`    | all routes | --  | see below | -- | Per-route breakdown in HTTP table         |

Note: The internal `cipherbox_ipfs_ipns_duration_seconds` histogram values could not be extracted from the Grafana snapshot (new dashboard format does not embed query results for anonymous viewers). The per-route HTTP duration histogram below provides equivalent server-side timing data.

## HTTP API Performance (from Grafana dashboard)

Response Time by Route (p95) — mean and max over 6h window (12:30–18:30 UTC):

| Route                     | p95 Mean | p95 Max | Notes                                   |
| ------------------------- | -------- | ------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `POST /ipfs/upload`       | 328 ms   | 1.67 s  | Includes 1MB/5MB/10MB uploads           |
| `GET /ipfs/:cid`          | 9.50 ms  | 9.50 ms | Extremely fast server-side              |
| `GET /ipns/resolve`       | 286 ms   | 887 ms  | Includes DB cache fallback path         |
| `POST /ipns/publish`      | 860 ms   | 919 ms  | Slowest operation — Kubo IPNS publish   |
| `POST /ipns/publish-batch`| 813 ms   | 950 ms  | TEE republish batch path                |
| `GET /vault`              | 9.50 ms  | 9.50 ms |                                         |
| `GET /vault/quota`        | 9.50 ms  | 9.50 ms |                                         |
| `GET /health`             | 11.1 ms  | 48 ms   |                                         |
| `POST /auth/test-login`   | 177 ms   | 243 ms  |                                         |

Overall Response Time (all routes combined, from time-series chart):
- p50: ~10 ms (most routes are fast DB lookups)
- p95: ~300 ms (dominated by IPNS resolve)
- p99: ~900 ms (dominated by IPNS publish, spikes to ~3s under load)

## Kubo Health Observations

| Metric             | Value    | Notes                                                              |
| ------------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Peer Connections   | N/A      | Kubo v0.34.0 does not expose libp2p metrics to Prometheus          |
| Inbound Bandwidth  | N/A      | Grafana panel shows "No data"                                      |
| Outbound Bandwidth | N/A      | Grafana panel shows "No data"                                      |
| Memory Usage       | N/A      | Grafana panel shows "No data"                                      |
| Goroutines         | N/A      | Not exposed by Kubo                                                |
| Datastore Size     | ~320 MiB | From dashboard "Total Storage Used" stat (includes all user data)  |

## Stress Test Details

To populate IPNS publish histogram data, a manual stress test was performed via Playwright against the staging web app:

| Operation    | Count | Details                                                  |
| ------------ | ----- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Folder create| 8     | stress-01 through -05, nested-subfolder, rapid-fire-01–03|
| File upload  | 13    | 10 small (7–48 KB) + 3 large (1 MB, 5 MB, 10 MB)       |
| Rename       | 4     | 2 files, 1 folder, 1 large file                         |
| Move         | 3     | Files into stress-02, stress-03, renamed-folder-01       |
| Delete       | 10    | 5 files + 5 folders (some with contents)                 |
| **Total**    | **~38–43** | Each mutates metadata → IPNS publish                |

Concurrently, `baseline-benchmark.sh` ran 20 iterations of resolve/pin/cat (+ warmups).

## Notes

- Client-side timings captured 2026-03-07 via `baseline-benchmark.sh` (5 total runs, 100 data points)
- Server-side HTTP timings captured from Grafana Cloud dashboard snapshot at 18:30 UTC
- IPNS Publish is the dominant bottleneck at ~860ms p95 — this is Kubo's native IPNS publish latency
- Kubo v0.34.0 does not expose libp2p metrics — Kubo Health section is N/A
- TEE Republish Batch Duration shows "No data" — mock TEE provider doesn't report real durations
- These baselines will be compared against post-Phase 19 and Phase 22 measurements
- The benchmark script is deterministic: same iterations, same file size, same warmup count

## Comparison Target

Phase 22 (after IPFS infrastructure changes) will re-run this benchmark and document:

- Performance regression threshold: >20% p95 increase requires investigation
- Performance improvement targets vary by operation (see Phase 22 plan)
